ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a ring system in which a benzene ring is fused with a six-membered alicyclic ring; the upper-right position of the alicyclic ring is a ketone carbonyl C=O, and the lower part of the alicyclic ring is connected to an OSO2NH4/sulfonyloxy substituent; on the right there is :NH3 bearing a lone pair, and a curved arrow goes from the lone pair of ammonia to the carbonyl carbon. Reasoning: This arrow indicates ammonia acting as a nucleophile to attack the ketone carbonyl carbon, and the carbonyl carbon changes from a planar carbonyl center to a tetrahedral center; according to the state after this electron transfer, the original C=O becomes C(OH), and at the same time this carbon is newly connected to N, while the connection relationships of the fused aromatic ring skeleton and the OSO2NH4 substituent remain unchanged. Writing this product connection relationship as a SMILES gives NOS(OC1CC(O)(N)Cc2c1cccc2)=O.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the starting molecule as a benzene-fused cyclohexanone bearing an OSO2NH4 substituent, plus free ammonia with a lone pair. Use the arrow to locate the reaction center: ammonia attacks the ketone carbonyl carbon. Replace the carbonyl C=O unit by a tetrahedral C bearing both O/H as OH and an N substituent from ammonia, while preserving the fused aromatic ring and the OSO2NH4 substituent connectivity. Translate this product connectivity into the required SMILES, yielding NOS(OC1CC(O)(N)Cc2c1cccc2)=O.
